counterfactual_missing_items: No raw evidence of broad, nonseptate hyphae with right-angle branching, which would support mucormycosis.
decisive_items: Methenamine silver staining revealed yeast-like structures associated with septate hyphae demonstrating acute-angle branching.
Histopathologic analysis showed diffuse necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and fungal elements.
Chest CT (lung window) showed cavitary and noncavitary nodules and masses with faint surrounding ground-glass opacity (“halo sign”)
response.rationale: R1 is directly supported by pathognomonic fungal morphology on methenamine silver staining: yeast-like structures with septate hyphae demonstrating acute-angle branching, alongside necrotizing granulomatous inflammation and cavitary nodules with halo sign. R4 shares nonspecific imaging and granulomatous fungal inflammation but is contradicted by the same fungal morphology, which favors Aspergillus rather than Mucorales.

rejected.why: Mucormycosis is disconfirmed by the raw finding of septate hyphae with acute-angle branching; mucormycosis would instead show broad, nonseptate hyphae with right-angle branching.
